correctness.rationale: The affine field integrates exactly to the first-ray-crossing equation omega*t-1=s*((b+1)*exp(-k*t)-b), with b=alpha-mu*Delta/k. At mu*=k/Delta*(alpha-q/(1-q)), t=1/omega is the unique locally selected root for all small s; all calibrated sector times are constant. Exact second-order Taylor differentiation yields the gain-Jacobian columns (Q_i B_i,-Q_i B_i R_i). Since R_i/(Q_i q_i)=c_i/(1-exp(-c_i))>1>c_{i+1}/(exp(c_{i+1})-1)=R_{i+1}/(Q_i q_i), every R_i>R_{i+1}, and all ordered 2x2 minors are positive. The inverse-function theorem applies locally. Independent original affine-flow endpoint and finite-difference diagnostics passed in the bundled checker; they are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the universal strict positivity of every ordered two-gain minor for the first two near-cycle return-clock Taylor coefficients. Full-text inspection of Kai (2026) confirms it supplies the affine oscillator and known period/stability but not the all-pair two-jet rank law. A fully read prior global conjugacy result has a distinct radial calibration; a fully read regular-polygon result treats scalar first-exit and central startup. The different hypotheses and conclusions do not imply the new theorem. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches returned no equivalent or stronger all-parameter theorem. Priority remains provisional because older synthesis and general nonlinear phase sensitivity literature is incompletely accessible.
residual_risks: The older 2012 and 2019 polygonal-affine oscillator papers have not been fully read; historical priority against an undocumented coefficient extension is not certified.
Other nonlinear phase-response and return-time sensitivity analyses, possibly under different terminology, may contain equivalent or stronger joint two-jet controllability.
Search coverage and current published records are not a mathematical proof of novelty. Independent specialist literature review remains open.

value.rationale: The two transverse Taylor coefficients of the physical return time are natural first- and second-order timing responses important for synchronization and pulse sensitivity. The exact all-pair minor theorem provides a robust constructive ability to steer both with any two tangential gains for arbitrary polygons and heterogeneous positive rates, while the prescribed cycle, physical period, and Floquet stability stay fixed. This goes beyond the previously established qualitative tangential freedom, global radial conjugacy at another gain, or a single-sector first-exit formula. The result is local, and no downstream claims beyond this meaningful structural control statement are made.
